prompt.context_jp: 夜の東京を見下ろす窓に、根尾光誠の顔___薄く映っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 夜の東京を見下ろす窓に、根尾光誠の顔___薄く映っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this opening scene.

feedback.correct_en: This is the opening sentence of the chapter. The reflection is new information being introduced to the reader, so が is natural — it marks what newly appears on scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat 根尾光誠の顔 as already-known topic, which doesn't fit a scene-opening description. を doesn't work with the intransitive 映っていた.

contrast_examples.en: A face was reflected in the window. (newly perceived)

contrast_examples.jp: その顔は窓に映っていた。
contrast_examples.en: That face (which we were discussing) was reflected in the window.

prompt.context_jp: 背中を押されて落ちたはずのその男___、いま別の若者の体を借りて生きている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 背中を押されて落ちたはずのその男___、いま別の若者の体を借りて生きている。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle sets up this man as the topic being described?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence frames 'that man' as the known topic (established in sentence 1) and then comments on his situation. は marks the topic for this characterization.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present him as fresh new information, but he was just introduced. The sentence is explaining his state, not identifying who did something.

contrast_examples.jp: その男は今も生きている。
contrast_examples.en: That man is still alive. (topic + comment)

prompt.context_jp: NEOXISの応接室では、東郷___窓辺に立ち、パリ行きの搭乗券を指の間で回していた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 東郷___窓辺に立ち、パリ行きの搭乗券を指の間で回していた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits as the scene shifts to a new location?

feedback.correct_en: The scene has just shifted to the NEOXIS reception room. Togo is introduced as the figure present in the new scene — が marks this scene-setting presence.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply Togo is the already-established topic, but we're newly placing him in this scene. で marks location, not the person.

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋に男が立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: A man was standing in the room. (scene-setting)

contrast_examples.jp: その男は部屋に立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: The man was standing in the room. (comment on known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 根尾光誠の声___、彼にとって唯一の道しるべになりつつある。
prompt.prompt_jp: 根尾光誠の声___、彼にとって唯一の道しるべになりつつある。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for making a general characterization?

feedback.correct_en: This is a characterizing statement about Neo's voice as a known entity. は sets it up as the topic for a general description of its role for Togo.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it sound like identifying 'which thing is the guide' among options; here we're commenting on an established subject.

contrast_examples.en: It's his voice that encourages me. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: テレビ画面には、パリの惨劇を伝える速報___流れ続けていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: テレビ画面には、パリの惨劇を伝える速報___流れ続けていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle fitting this scene-description.

feedback.correct_en: The breaking-news report appears as something present/perceivable on the screen — a newly described element of the scene. が fits this existential/descriptive use.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would wrongly imply the news report was already an established topic. The focus is on what fills the screen as part of the setting.

contrast_examples.jp: 画面にニュースが流れていた。
contrast_examples.en: News was running on the screen. (scene detail)

contrast_examples.jp: そのニュースは画面に流れていた。
contrast_examples.en: That news (we were talking about) was running on the screen.

prompt.context_jp: 部屋の隅の柱時計___、静かに時を刻む。
prompt.prompt_jp: 部屋の隅の柱時計___、静かに時を刻む。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for a sensory background detail?

feedback.correct_en: The clock is a background element newly brought into the reader's perception during the silence. が marks it as a fresh perceptual detail.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would suggest the clock was already being discussed. Here it's a sensory image emerging in a quiet moment.

contrast_examples.en: A clock ticks away the time. (perceived)

prompt.context_jp: 誰も口を開かない数秒のあいだに、部屋の空気の温度___すっと下がった気がした。
prompt.prompt_jp: 部屋の空気の温度___すっと下がった気がした。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for this sudden sensation?

feedback.correct_en: The drop in temperature is a newly-noticed sensation inside the subordinate clause. が marks it as the new information being perceived.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the temperature as the known topic, but here it's the fresh perception the narrator just registered.

contrast_examples.en: Air is a heavy thing. (general topic)

prompt.context_jp: 夕暮れどきの惣菜屋の店先に、秀子___コロッケの油鍋を覗き込んでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 夕暮れどきの惣菜屋の店先に、秀子___コロッケの油鍋を覗き込んでいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits introducing a character into a new scene?

feedback.correct_en: A new scene opens at the deli at dusk. Hideko is newly presented within this setting, so が marks her existence/presence in the fresh scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would require Hideko to already be the running topic, but we have just changed scene.

contrast_examples.jp: 店先に女性が立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: A woman was standing at the storefront.

prompt.context_jp: 秀子___皿を拭く手を止め、英治___缶ビールを持ったまま画面を見つめた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 秀子___皿を拭く手を止め、英治___缶ビールを持ったまま画面を見つめた。
prompt.prompt_en: Both blanks take the same particle. Which contrasts the two characters' simultaneous reactions?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence pairs two subjects doing parallel actions. は on both marks each as the topic of its own clause and sets up the contrastive 'as for X... as for Y...' structure.
feedback.incorrect_en: Double が would read as two separate exclamations of new information, which doesn't match this reflective dual portrait. も would mean 'also,' adding an unintended inclusive meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: 母は料理し、父は新聞を読む。
contrast_examples.en: Mother cooks, father reads the paper. (contrastive)

contrast_examples.jp: 母が料理し、父が新聞を読む。
contrast_examples.en: Mother cooks and father reads (foregrounding each action as event).

prompt.context_jp: 一萬田___目を上げず、指先で書類の角だけを撫でている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 一萬田___目を上げず、指先で書類の角だけを撫でている。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for describing Ichimanda's ongoing behavior?

feedback.correct_en: Ichimanda is the established figure in the Soman meeting scene. は marks him as the topic for this behavioral description.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight him as new/exclusive, but this is a quiet characterization of a known character.

contrast_examples.jp: 社長は何も言わなかった。
社長が何も言わなかった。
contrast_examples.en: It was the president who said nothing. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 勝った___、確かに商店街の側だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 勝った___、確かに商店街の側だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle produces the cleft-like 'the one who won was...' nuance?

feedback.correct_en: のは…だった is the standard cleft structure: 'As for the one who won, it was the shopping street side.' The topic (what won) is introduced for comment.
feedback.incorrect_en: のが…だった would reverse the information structure and sound unnatural here where '勝った方' is treated as the known/presupposed topic.

contrast_examples.en: The one who came was Tanaka.

prompt.context_jp: 根尾光誠は自分の心臓の音___、少し早くなっているのに気づく。
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分の心臓の音___、少し早くなっているのに気づく。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits inside the subordinate clause of noticing?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a 〜のに気づく clause, the thing noticed is new perceived information. が marks the heartbeat as the newly-registered subject of that embedded perception.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside a subordinate 'notice that...' clause is unusual because the clause introduces fresh content, not a topic to comment on. を doesn't fit the intransitive 早くなっている.

contrast_examples.jp: 手が震えているのに気づいた。
contrast_examples.en: I noticed my hand was trembling.

prompt.context_jp: 根尾光誠___、その男の輪郭に、なぜか胸を騒がせていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 根尾光誠___、その男の輪郭に、なぜか胸を騒がせていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the viewpoint character.

feedback.correct_en: Neo Kosei is the ongoing POV character of the scene. は presents him as the topic whose inner state is being narrated.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight him exclusively ('it was Neo who...'), which doesn't fit this inner-monologue style narration.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は心を揺さぶられた。
彼が心を揺さぶられた。
contrast_examples.en: It was he who was shaken. (contrasted with others)

prompt.context_jp: 英治の顔からは血の気___引き、ぐい呑みは空のまま卓に伏せられている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 英治の顔からは血の気___引き、...
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits inside this descriptive clause?

feedback.correct_en: 血の気が引く is a set expression where 血の気 is the subject newly undergoing the change. が marks this subject within the fixed collocation.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would awkwardly topicalize blood-color in a double-は sentence (顔からは…血の気は…), creating heavy, unnatural stacking.

contrast_examples.jp: 顔から血の気が引いた。
contrast_examples.en: The color drained from his face. (set phrase)

prompt.context_jp: こういう場面での気配り___、社長時代には苦手としてきた領域だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: こういう場面での気配り___、社長時代には苦手としてきた領域だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces 'this kind of attentiveness' as the topic?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence makes a general reflective statement defining what 気配り was for him. は topicalizes the concept so the predicate '…な領域だった' can characterize it.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present it as new identificational info; を doesn't fit a copular 'X は Y だ' structure.

contrast_examples.jp: 細かい気配りは私の苦手だ。
contrast_examples.en: Fine attentiveness is my weak point. (definition)

contrast_examples.jp: 細かい気配りが必要だ。

prompt.context_jp: 予定変更の裏に自分の助言が働いていることを思うと、口の中___わずかに苦くなった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 口の中___わずかに苦くなった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this emotional idiom about a bitter taste?

feedback.correct_en: 口の中が苦くなる is a set emotional idiom (feeling bitter/uneasy). The 'inside of the mouth' is the subject undergoing the change, so が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame '口の中' as a topic being contrasted; で would wrongly mark it as a location where something else became bitter.

prompt.context_jp: かつて立ち退きの___立たされていた男の顔が、今は柔らかく緩んでいる。
prompt.prompt_jp: かつて立ち退きの___立たされていた男の顔が…
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes '立たされていた' to mean 'forced into the front line of'?

feedback.correct_en: 矢面に立たされる is a fixed idiom meaning 'to be forced into the line of fire/front of criticism.' It fits Tsuchiya's position during the eviction pressure.
feedback.incorrect_en: 表面に立つ or 正面に立つ are not idiomatic for 'bearing the brunt.' Only 矢面 (literally 'arrow-face') carries this metaphor.

contrast_examples.en: He bore the brunt of criticism.
He stood at the front (literal position).

prompt.context_jp: 便宜と資本とをちらつかせ、法の網目のなかで相手を消耗させていく——それが 一萬田の___だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: それが 一萬田の___だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word means 'standard/habitual tactic'?

feedback.correct_en: 常套 (じょうとう) means a habitual or stock tactic — exactly fitting Ichimanda's go-to method of attrition.
feedback.incorrect_en: 常識 means 'common sense' (not a tactic); 常任 means 'permanent/standing' (as in a committee role).

contrast_examples.jp: それが彼の常套手段だ。

prompt.context_jp: しかし彼の胸には、勝利感よりもむしろ、ある種の___が澱のように残っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ある種の___が澱のように残っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word captures the lingering guilty feeling?

feedback.correct_en: 後ろめたさ means 'a feeling of guilt / uneasy conscience,' which fits Neo's conflicted sense of having used foreknowledge unfairly.
feedback.incorrect_en: 後回し means 'putting off / postponing'; 後ろ姿 is a 'back view (of a person).' Neither describes a feeling.

prompt.context_jp: 家の中はいっとき、蒼萬との争いも借金も忘れたような温もりに___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 家の中は…温もりに___。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb completes 'enveloped in warmth'?

feedback.correct_en: 〜に包まれる ('enveloped in / wrapped in') is the natural collocation with atmospheric nouns like 温もり, 静けさ, 匂い.
feedback.incorrect_en: 縛られる (be tied) and 塗られる (be painted) don't collocate with 温もり.

prompt.context_jp: 地震という圧倒的な現実の前では、契約書の細字も交渉のかけひきも しばし ___見える。
prompt.prompt_jp: ...しばし ___見える。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb means 'to look blurred/faded' in the face of overwhelming reality?

feedback.correct_en: かすむ means 'to grow dim / fade / become hazy.' Negotiations 'fade from view' when compared with the earthquake's reality.
feedback.incorrect_en: すむ ('to end') and すかす ('to see through') don't produce the required 'hazy, diminished' nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: 問題がかすんで見えた。

prompt.context_jp: スケジュールは経団連会長のひと言で___を立てて崩れかけていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ...ひと言で___を立てて崩れかけていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits with 立てて to mean 'noisily collapse'?

feedback.correct_en: 音を立てて is a set adverbial phrase meaning 'noisily / with a sound.' Here it dramatizes the schedule's audible collapse.
feedback.incorrect_en: 声を立てる is used for voices/laughs, not for a schedule falling apart. 波を立てる means 'to make waves (literal or figurative discord).'

prompt.context_jp: 「もし仮に 僕が あなたの息子だったら こう言うでしょうね “今すぐ 僕の世界から___ください”」
prompt.prompt_jp: “今すぐ 僕の世界から___ください”
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb completes the cold dismissal 'get out of my world'?

feedback.correct_en: 〜から消えてください ('disappear from...') is the sharp, cutting dismissal Neo delivers — matching his cold business persona here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 降りて ('get off') suits vehicles; 逃げて ('run away') implies the hearer is in danger, not a command to vanish from someone's life.

prompt.context_jp: Chapter opening scene — Neo gazes out over nighttime Tokyo.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing opens the scene more naturally as literary narration?

choices.text: 夜の東京を見下ろす窓に、根尾光誠の顔が薄く映っていた。
根尾光誠の顔は、夜の東京を見下ろす窓に薄く映っていた。

feedback.correct_en: Starting with the setting phrase (〜窓に) and then introducing the person with が is a classic literary opening — it eases the reader into the scene before revealing the character.
feedback.incorrect_en: Version B topicalizes Neo's face first, which presumes the reader already knows him. It works mid-story but is heavier as an opening line.

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋の隅に、男が立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: In the corner of the room, a man was standing. (natural opener)

contrast_examples.jp: 男は部屋の隅に立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: The man was standing in the corner. (presupposes known man)
